# Capitoline Museums

> > The world's first public museum, founded by Pope Sixtus IV in 1471, housing masterpieces by Caravaggio, Michelangelo, and Titian alongside ancient Roman sculptures in Palazzo dei Conservatori and Palazzo Nuovo on Rome's Capitoline Hill.

The Capitoline Museums offer visitors access to an extraordinary collection of ancient sculptures including the Capitoline Venus, Dying Gaul, and Boy with Thorn, plus Renaissance and Baroque paintings in the Pinacoteca Capitolina. Located in Piazza del Campidoglio, the museum complex provides comprehensive visitor information including tickets, guided tours, accessibility services, and practical planning resources.
